newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to start Treasury Bond issue in March.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to start Treasury Bond issue in March.

text.p: Sri Lanka will begin issuing Treasury Bonds in March to address the need for long-term debt instruments, a Central Bank official said on Monday.
"We will begin (issuing) in the first week of March, when hopefully the infrastructure and legal framework will be ready," a Public Debt official of the Central Bank told Reuters.

The Central Bank informed primary dealers last week that Treasury Bonds will be first issued with a two-year maturity and auctioned every two weeks. Each issue will be for 500 million rupees, the official said.
The interest rate, which will be market determined, will be based on a coupon rate of 15 percent. The issues will be underwritten by the Employees Provident Fund.
The Central Bank first floated the idea of issuing Treasury Bonds in August 1996.
Infrastructure for Central Bank operations was badly hit when its headquarters was damaged in a suspected separatist bombing on January 31, 1996.
Sri Lanka has long suffered from a lack of transferable long-term securities.
The only government debt instruments which are currently transferable by endorsement are three, six and 12-month Treasury Bills.
Government securities of two-year, five- to six-year and seven- to eight-year maturities are cumbersome and not easily transferable.
Sri Lankan borrowers have welcomed the issue, saying it will help to develop a yield curve of over one year.
